A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Self-Transcendence, with matching authors, the same central training framework, and corresponding ImageNet experiments despite the changed title. All supplied pages, including v2's supplementary sections, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation results, component and hyperparameter ablations, feature analyses, and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original ImageNet experiments and adds text-to-image results, a one-stage training comparison, and GPU-memory measurements.

M1.justification: The narrative retains VAE warm-up, a frozen guiding model, feature-level classifier-free guidance, and early stopping; VAE Structure Guidance renames VAE-based alignment. However, v2's Eq. (3) drops parentheses that materially change the guidance rule. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an intended procedure change or a typesetting error.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual text-to-image generation with MMDiT in Section 10/Table 8, extending evaluation beyond class-conditioned generation. Figure 8 identifies MS-COCO for the qualitative examples, although the training dataset is not named locally. ImageNet 256×256 and 512×512 coverage is retained; the latter moves to the supplement.

E2.justification: v2 adds vanilla MMDiT as a comparator in the text-to-image experiment and an EMA-based one-stage variant in Table 6. The existing ImageNet comparator sets remain unchanged; REPA also participates in the new text-to-image comparison.

E3.justification: The training-cost comparison changes its stated budget from 200 epochs/1 million iterations to 400 epochs/2 million iterations and adds peak GPU memory as a measurement. New experiments specify 150,000 iterations for MMDiT and an 80-epoch, 50,000-sample one-stage comparison. These are reported setting additions or revisions, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 6/Table 6 adds a focused test of two-stage training against joint training with an updated EMA teacher. Figure 2 revises the proposed method's feature-separability visualization and scores. Existing component, hyperparameter, early-stopping, and layerwise feature analyses are largely retained, with several relocated to the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The same-seed control for qualitative training comparisons is retained. Changed logistic-regression accuracies in Figure 2 are result changes, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports text-to-image FIDs of 6.23, 4.90, and 4.56 for MMDiT, REPA, and Self-Transcendence at 150,000 iterations. Table 6 adds one-stage FID 34.50 versus two-stage 20.49. Figure 2 changes Self-Transcendence FID from 22.30 to 20.49 and classification accuracy from 0.9804 to 0.9961, crossing REPA's unchanged 0.9882. The 300K-teacher ablation changes from FID/IS 22.91/71.32 to 23.05/70.32, and the loss-weight discussion corrects 23.91 to 22.91. Cost results use a longer budget and add memory values. Main ImageNet comparison tables retain their scores.

T1.justification: The printed definition in Eq. (3) changes from f_u + omega*(f_c - f_u) to f_u + omega*f_c - f_u, which simplifies to omega*f_c. This is mathematically inequivalent, although its intent is unresolved. Other equation edits are equivalent notation changes; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim that internal guidance can match or surpass externally guided REPA is retained. v2 expands the abstract's demonstrated scope to both class-to-image and text-to-image generation; v1 treated text-to-image applicability as future work.

C2.justification: v2 adds a task-dependent hyperparameter-tuning limitation and interprets the one-stage variant's weakness as unreliable early EMA guidance. Its applicability boundary becomes image generation generally. The new claim of smaller memory overhead than REPA needs qualification: Table 5 reports a higher initial peak, 12.34 versus 10.39 GB, followed by lower memory after early stopping.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly specifies three linear MLP layers with two SiLU activations, documenting the existing alignment component. v2 also discloses peak memory requirements. Conversely, the explicit 512×512 preprocessing description using 64×64×4 Stable Diffusion VAE latents is replaced by a reference to REPA's pipeline. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Singh et al., 'What Matters for Representation Alignment: Global Information or Spatial Structure?' as reference 37 and connects it to the structural-guidance motivation. The established positioning against external guidance and existing self-contained methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the title, abstract, introduction, and explanatory passages, emphasizing structurally clean and semantically discriminative guidance. It renames the first stage and reorganizes early stopping, high-resolution experiments, and feature visualization into an explicitly introduced supplementary section.

P2.justification: The two-column design becomes predominantly single-column with wrapped tables and a redesigned title/abstract. Figure 1 swaps panel groups, Figure 2 changes from a grid to a horizontal arrangement, and Figure 3 merges the framework with the former Figure 4 learning curve. New cost, one-stage, and text-to-image tables and a text-to-image figure accompany extensive relocation of retained displays.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence for text-to-image applicability and the two-stage design, plus MLP and memory disclosures. However, Eq. (3) introduces an unresolved ambiguity in the central method specification. The revised cost comparison also reports 58.87 hours where its stated speed and budget imply 59.87, and its broad memory advantage needs qualification. These gains in validation coexist with regressions in mathematical accuracy and resource interpretation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
